next_quarter_outlook.topic: FY28 dark-store expansion upgrade
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management confirms a more aggressive store-addition target with a higher FY28 run-rate than FY27; most new stores will be in smaller cities where paybacks are performing well.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "On the quick commerce business, the new store addition targets that you've laid out are more aggressive than they have been in the past and imply a higher run rate of store additions in FY28 versus FY27." ... "That's right, Garima. Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on, and we are seeing great outcomes in terms of payback on these stores in these markets that we've expanded into in the last few quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal
next_quarter_outlook.location: Transcript pages 2–3 (PDF pages 3–4); analyst question followed by management confirmation

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Blinkit growth acceleration from December
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management explicitly says Blinkit NOV growth should accelerate year-on-year beginning in the December quarter.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "And just to push on that, you're talking about NOV growth pickup starting the December quarter on a YoY basis?" ... "That's right."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal
next_quarter_outlook.location: Transcript page 7 (PDF page 8); analyst clarification confirmed by management

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Blinkit margins
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Accelerating store additions from OND are not expected to reduce margins in the short term; management expects longer-term expansion.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, it was a specific comment. What we are saying here is that as we accelerate store addition, which is starting OND, we don't expect that to hit the margins in the short term. Longer term, of course, margins will continue expanding, but we don't expect that there should be a short-term margin reduction on account of accelerated store addition."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Blinkit store productivity
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management still sees steady-state NOV per store rising toward about ₹11 lakh per day from ₹9 lakh, though rapid store additions may make the quarterly path uneven.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Basis what we know today, yes, we think NOV per day should go up. We gave guidance last time that in steady state it could get to about INR 11 lakh per day per store. We are at INR 9 lakh today. We do think it will go up directionally over time, but there could be some quarters where the growth in the number of stores is lumpy, and therefore it may not be linearly upwards."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Food-delivery reinvestment
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Food-delivery margins are expected to stay broadly flat for one to two years as operating leverage is reinvested to expand the market and absolute adjusted EBITDA.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards. That's what the operating principle is. It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

next_quarter_outlook.topic: dark.ai launch and economics
next_quarter_outlook.summary: dark.ai is a few months from launch; the base case is a high-gross-margin, largely self-funded business that could reach profitability relatively quickly, while the next 12 months should reveal whether it becomes meaningful.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "As a base case, we think this could be a high gross margin business, which could fund itself largely and get to profitability pretty soon. That's the outlook right now. It's very early." ... "We expect the next 12 months to tell us whether any of this will become meaningful."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Akshant Goyal

analyst_focus.topic: How aggressive can Blinkit expansion become without hurting returns?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts repeatedly asked about the upgraded FY28 store plan, smaller-city paybacks, capex per store, competitive visibility, NOV per store and whether accelerated additions would pressure margins.

analyst_focus.topic: Where will growth and margins settle across food delivery and Blinkit?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts pressed on December-quarter Blinkit NOV acceleration, the FY29 adjusted-EBITDA target, food-delivery growth, reinvestment and the durability of margin expansion.

key_risks: A faster dark-store rollout can make store productivity and cash deployment uneven across quarters.
Food-delivery operating leverage is being reinvested, keeping percentage margins broadly flat for one to two years.

evidence.speaker: Garima Mishra and Akshant Goyal

There will be furloughs that will impact the H2, there will be lower working day s and all of those implications and all of those impacts. So that will definitely be there. And like always, we do not have one model that leads to guidance. There are always multiple models that leads to mult iple points of the guidance. At the lower end of the guidance, we have baked in higher uncertainty at the upper end of the guidance, we have baked in an improvement in the environment. next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Nidhu Saxena

next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Nidhu Saxena

analyst_focus.topic: Minimum wages and delivery-centre footprint
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Karnataka and Telangana wage hikes hit margins; analysts asked whether a stay creates upside and why the delivery-centre count and lease assets fell (answer: site consolidation and counting change).

analyst_focus.topic: Will easing payer medical costs reduce cost pressure on vendors?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Payer margins improved in H1 2026; analysts asked if that gives Sagility pricing relief, and management said cost take-out pressure persists.

analyst_focus.topic: What is in the $40 million ACV and what M&A comes next?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts sought payer versus provider mix, deal duration and margins, and remaining capability gaps for further acquisitions; the segment split was not available.

analyst_focus.topic: What does the low double-digit guidance include?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Clarified that guidance is organic only, with CareSeed and Chirok additive.

key_risks: Open enrolment and AEP revenue is expected flat to slightly lower year on year, pressuring the seasonal peak.
Margin upgrade assumes FX stays at current levels and efficiency gains persist.
AI-driven productivity gains are largely passed through to clients, capping structural margin upside and keeping client cost pressure high.
Provider organic revenue has been weak (discrete project taper at one client) and Chirok was acquired only a day before the call, so integration and AI disruption of coding are open risks.
Karnataka and Telangana minimum-wage increases are in guidance; a reversal is upside but the current impact is a cost headwind.

material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Both ends of the range raised by 100 bps
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management states it is raising FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from 24-25% to 25-26%.

evidence.speaker: Ramesh Gopalan
evidence.quote: "we are raising our FY '27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance from our earlier 24% to 25% to a new 25% to 26%."

AXISBANK.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: NIM uplift expected from Q3 as FCNR(B) funds retire costly NRTDs
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The 11 bps FCNR(B) drag was a one-quarter optics effect; part of the funds already retired expensive non-resident term deposits late in Q2, so Q3 should see NIM benefit, while the through-cycle 3.8% NIM guidance is unchanged.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So we should be able to see some benefit of that come through in the next quarter in terms of NIM uplift."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Q3 and Q4 to show NIM benefit from balance-sheet optimisation
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Redeploying FCNR(B) funds into loans and retiring higher-cost liabilities is expected to lift NIM over the next two quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I think in Q3 and Q4, you should be able to see some sort of a benefit coming through due to the optimization exercise that we'll be doing."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Sequential NIM improvement intended, but no firm timeline
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management wants NIM to move up each quarter via asset mix, liability mix and rate hikes, with some headwinds, and declines to call a time frame.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But sequentially, we should be able to show an improvement going forward."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Card fee weakness partly a festive-timing shift into October
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Year-on-year fee growth was weak because the festive spend month moved from September last year to October this year, implying some catch-up in Q3.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "last year, September was when the festive month had started. This year, that has shifted to October. So, there is a bit of a temporal difference on account of that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Subrat Mohanty

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Latest repo-rate increase flows through loan yields in Q4, not Q3
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank reprices its repo-linked book in the last week of the quarter, so the book-wide benefit of the latest repo hike lands in Q4; only new repo-linked loans reprice sooner.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So the latest repo rate increase from a book stock perspective, the benefit we will actually see in Q4 as opposed to in Q3."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Credit costs expected to improve further, no numeric guidance
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Slippage ratios and recoveries are improving in individual portfolios; part of the improvement is mix-driven, and the bank will not guide a credit cost number.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But directionally, what I can confirm is that we are on the trajectory towards improvement. I think there is some further improvement that also we can expect."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Bancassurance: draft IRDA commission rules likely 6-9 months away
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank expects regulation to take time, possibly with a glide path, and plans to mitigate through volumes, product mix and other fee sources; it will not quantify the impact.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I think we might get about 6 to 9 months before that comes through. So, we'll try and mitigate the impact during that point of time."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Subrat Mohanty

next_quarter_outlook.topic: FCNR(B) liquidity not fully deployed, leaving growth runway
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Part of the incremental FCNR(B) liability is still unused for asset growth while LCR is held in a 115-120% band, so loan growth can run ahead of deposit raising in coming quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we have not used the full FCNR (B) liquidity to grow our assets, right? So to that extent, there is runway for the balance sheet to grow"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Neeraj Gambhir

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Labour-code costs may recur if new guidelines arrive
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The Q2 one-offs included labour-code provisions on outsourced staff and ESIC; management says known items are covered but the area is evolving.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So far, based on what we have been aware of, we have already taken those into accounts. But this is an area where, you know, some new guidelines, etcetera, whenever they come, we will have to deal with that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Second-half posture: watchful on geopolitics, inflation, tariffs and weather
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CEO flags West Asia tensions, commodity prices and weather risks while expressing confidence in sustainable and profitable growth.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "As we enter second half of the year, we continue to remain watchful and closely monitor the evolving external environment."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Amitabh Chaudhry

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Through-cycle NIM target of 3.8% unchanged, no timeline given
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management will not say how long it takes to get to 3.8% from 3.36% (3.47% ex-FCNR).
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Though structurally, we are working towards our through-cycle guidance of 3.8% that we have mentioned earlier."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: ECL transition: no material impact expected, backed by ~INR 8,000 cr contingent provisions
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Both the transition and the subsequent flow are expected to be non-material for FY28, with floor rates for stage 1 and 2 still being worked through.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we don't expect any material impact to come through on the transition itself. This is also supported because we have existing contingent provisions almost close to 8,000 crores that continue"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Loan growth guided at 300 bps above industry over the medium term
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The medium-term growth guidance is reiterated as the base for NII; no specific NII number is given.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We have guided for 300 basis points higher than the industry average over the medium term."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Retail share of loans to be rebuilt towards above 55%
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Corporate has outgrown retail; management says it is working to stop the retail mix slipping further and to return above 55% as retail book growth catches up with disbursements.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we get back to the above 55% retail mix. So that effort is on at this point in time."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Subrat Mohanty

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Corporate lending growth described as diversified and sustainable
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Growth is spread across capex, project finance, refinancing and working capital with selective origination; downstream salary and liability benefits are cited.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So corporate growth is sustainable because it's well diversified across sector segments and financing categories."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Vijay Mulbagal
next_quarter_outlook.role: Bank executive (role not stated in transcript)

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Cost-to-assets expected to keep falling once one-offs fall away
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The Q2 cost-to-assets uptick on a quarterly basis is attributed to one-timers (labour code and FCNR costs); management expects the ratio to fall further adjusted for these.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I think this is primarily due to the one-timers that we have seen in the cost for this quarter. That's why I think, adjusted for that, you will see the ratio coming down even further."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

next_quarter_outlook.topic: UPI MDR revenue upside cannot be sized; implementation postponed
next_quarter_outlook.summary: The bank plays across issuing, PSP and acquiring roles but gives no revenue guidance and may reinvest part of any MDR revenue into the ecosystem.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "at this stage, we can't give any specific guidance because the MDR implementation has been postponed."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Arnika Dixit
next_quarter_outlook.role: Bank executive (role not stated in transcript)

next_quarter_outlook.topic: No equity capital needed for growth or protection
next_quarter_outlook.summary: CET1 at 14.61% plus ~49 bps of unreckoned provision buffer; management rules out equity raising.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We reiterate that we do not need equity capital for either the growth or protection pillars."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Rajeev Mantri

analyst_focus.topic: Has NIM bottomed, and what is the exit rate and path from here?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Five analysts pressed on NIM: reported 3.36% was down 37 bps YoY with an 11 bps FCNR(B) distortion. They tested whether Q2 is the trough, the September exit NIM, how the FCNR drag unwinds, and the Q4 timing of repo-hike repricing; management declined monthly NIM and a firm timeline.

analyst_focus.topic: Will corporate keep out-growing retail, and is that growth durable?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Retail share fell below the previously signalled 55% as wholesale grew 34% YoY; analysts asked if the mix would keep shifting given wide AA spreads and industry-wide FCNR-funded corporate lending.

analyst_focus.topic: Where do credit costs settle, including ECL and FY28?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Net credit cost fell to 0.45% after standard-asset provisions on FCNR loans; analysts asked about normalisation versus further improvement, unusual recoveries, and whether the ECL transition removes the ROA tailwind from lower credit costs in FY28.

analyst_focus.topic: Why is fee growth weak and what do regulatory changes do to it?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Fee grew only 6% YoY on cards, payments and asset-linked fee dilution; analysts asked about the draft IRDA bancassurance guidelines, how to offset them, the UPI MDR opportunity and any fee on FCNR mobilisation (none charged).

analyst_focus.topic: Is operating leverage real once one-offs are stripped out?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Opex rose 11% QoQ and cost-to-assets looked higher on a quarterly basis; analysts asked about the INR 254 cr one-offs (labour code, FCNR) and whether further jaws are available.

analyst_focus.topic: Has the FCNR(B) money been fully deployed, and what does that mean for liquidity?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: A back-of-envelope check showed INR 1 trillion raised against INR 80,000 cr net deposit growth and INR 68,000 cr loan growth with LCR flat near 119%; analysts asked how much room is left to grow and why run-off rates rose.

analyst_focus.topic: Personal loan strategy and unsecured growth
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: With peers growing PL faster, an analyst asked whether the bank would extend PL beyond salaried borrowers; management said PL stays salaried-only and self-employed borrowers go through business loans.

analyst_focus.topic: How will NII momentum evolve?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: NII growth accelerated to 5% QoQ; analysts asked whether the rate hike and FCNR deployment will extend it; no NII guidance was given.

analyst_focus.topic: ECLGS disbursement scale
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Analysts sized the government-guaranteed emergency line exposure: around 12,500 loans for INR 10,700 cr sanctioned, about 80% disbursed.

key_risks: Management will not give a timeline for NIM recovery to 3.8% and NIM still depends on FCNR(B) deployment and mix.
Fee growth is weak (6% YoY); draft IRDA bancassurance rules and uncertain UPI MDR add regulatory fee risk.
Retail share of loans has slipped below the 55% level management still wants to return to.
Labour-code related expense is described as an evolving area that could produce further one-offs.
Geopolitical tension in West Asia, commodity inflation, tariffs and weather risks are explicitly flagged for the second half.

TORNTPHARM.description: Company-website transcript linked from the NSE covering letter (user-approved source exception).

next_quarter_outlook.topic: JB margin improvement to continue for the next two to three quarters
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Q1-to-Q2 JB margin gains came mainly from field-force merger savings; the same run-rate of improvement is expected to continue.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I would expect quarter-on-quarter, this same run rate of improvement can continue maybe for the next two, three quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Germany: best case is a slight decline in coming quarters, stability after 3-4 quarters
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Loss of tenders, third-party supply disruption and government-mandated price cuts have hit the non-retail business; management declines to guide.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Best case, I would say slight decline in the coming quarters, and eventually some stability after maybe 3 or 4 quarters."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: INR 950-960 cr second tranche of the Novartis ophthalmology deal due in December
next_quarter_outlook.summary: A pending cash payment on the JB-Novartis ophthalmology portfolio is expected in the December quarter, which matters for net-debt trajectory (net debt/EBITDA now 1.8x).
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "there is a second tranche of payment of about INR950 crores, INR960 crores that is pending. Would that be due anytime soon? ... That would be in December of this year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Bino (Elara Capital); Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: JB India branded business to re-accelerate above 10% in H2
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After 13% in Q1 and 7% in Q2 (integration-hit), management expects gradual quarterly recovery and H2 JB India growth above the H1 average of 10%.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "if H1 is at 10% growth for the India branded business, I would expect that H2 should be perhaps higher than that."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Overall JB growth back to double digit in H2; international recovery slower
next_quarter_outlook.summary: JB international was down 7% in Q2 on plant-network and QC integration delays; management says the recovery may take longer but total JB should still return to double-digit growth in H2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So while the actions have been taken, the recovery may take slightly longer in the international business, but overall we still feel that in H2, the overall JB growth should be double-digit."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Group EBITDA margin to be a little above 33.5% in H2
next_quarter_outlook.summary: No numeric guidance, but management expects the second half to improve on Q2's 33.5%, with JB margins rising gradually for two to three more quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I think there should be a gradual increase in the EBITDA margin. But I think we're not guiding on the number part, but at least definitely we feel H2 should be little higher than 33.5%."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sudhir Menon

next_quarter_outlook.topic: US: four to five more filings this fiscal; price erosion rises in H2 from new competitors
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Filings of 9-10 products in the year will exceed several prior years, but management expects new competition on recent launches to raise pricing pressure in H2.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "we think we can file four to five at least more before this fiscal year ends. ... I expect some new competitors on our recent launches in H2."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Indian pharma market growth of at least 10% to persist through next financial year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: H1 market growth was about 12%; management sees it holding for the rest of this year and slipping only 1-2 points next year, calling this year potentially a one-off.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We think this market growth is likely to sustain for the rest of the year, and perhaps from next year it may drop a little bit, say 1%, 2%, but minimum 10% is what we think should continue from here on as well, at least for the next financial year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Curatio to sustain high growth for the rest of the year and likely a couple of years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Curatio grew 34% in Q2 and H1 and is now 7-8% of base India; management cannot say 30% growth lasts 3-5 years but sees the trend continuing.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "I think it should be possible to sustain high growth for at least a couple of years."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Brazil expected to keep growing mid-teens; Brazil generic semaglutide launch in 6-9 months
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Four business units are performing; 53 molecules await ANVISA approval over about three years; a first local generic semaglutide launch has expanded the market.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Brazil, we are optimistic, it'll continue to grow double-digit, mid-teens or something in that range"
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sanjay Gupta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: Field force held at 9,100 this year; possible 500 addition, 9,500-9,600 next year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: No headcount change this fiscal year after the field-force merger, with a possible base-business expansion later.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We expect potentially some expansion may be required in the base business, so say maybe by 500 MRs or so. But we're not fully certain on what the next year's picture looks like, but it could be say something between 9,500 to 9,600."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: INR 450 cr cost synergies now targeted in two years rather than three
next_quarter_outlook.summary: About half of the synergy is already in this year's margins and most comes through by next year; the INR 450 cr quantum is held and any upside will be reviewed in a couple of quarters.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "But directionally, yes, we've been able to achieve that much faster. Instead of three years, I think we should be able to get there in two years' time."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: India revenue synergies to start showing next year
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Cross-selling and adding JB brands to Torrent divisions typically take 6-12 months, with international synergies a longer 2-3 year journey.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "So, I think next year should see a reasonable improvement in the topline growth through revenue synergies."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: No FY28 margin guidance until Q1 FY28
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Management will wait for a full-year combined base before guiding FY28 EBITDA margins.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "No, we are not giving any guidance for FY28. We are just waiting for the full-year base to come in, and then probably next year quarter one, we will guide it."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Sudhir Menon

next_quarter_outlook.topic: R&D to stay at 4-4.5% of revenue for the next couple of years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: R&D is stepping up to lift US ANDA filings from low to high single digits a year; the Q2 increase is expected to persist, which caps margin expansion.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "We believe that the range should not exceed, say, between 4% to 4.5% even in the following year."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: India semaglutide: lost share to be recovered; generic market could reach INR 2,000-2,500 cr in 3-5 years
next_quarter_outlook.summary: After a roughly two-month injectable supply gap, supplies were fully restored in September; the analyst's estimate of a INR 2,000-2,500 cr market over three to five years was called 'not out of range'.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "Yes. That that should be possible. At least three to five years, that number is not out of range."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

next_quarter_outlook.topic: India semaglutide pricing expected stable to gradually higher
next_quarter_outlook.summary: Because the products are branded, management expects no per-patient price erosion despite rising competition.
next_quarter_outlook.evidence: "And in fact, the price would only be stable or gradually increase over the next couple of years."
next_quarter_outlook.speaker: Aman Mehta

analyst_focus.topic: How fast does JB recover, in India and internationally?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: JB revenue was flat YoY after integration; analysts asked whether the flat trend persists and whether international disruptions take longer to fix. Answer: India recovers gradually above 10% in H2; international slower; total double-digit in H2.

analyst_focus.topic: Are INR 450 cr cost synergies conservative, and when do revenue synergies come?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Roughly half appears already in margins; Neha Manpuria, Damayanti Kerai and Kunal Dhamesha tested upside, timing (two years versus three), and when revenue synergies start; management held the INR 450 cr number.

analyst_focus.topic: Where do group and JB EBITDA margins go from 33.5%?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Margin fell slightly QoQ (33.8% to 33.5%) as R&D rose 0.7 pts of revenue; analysts asked for JB margin parity with Torrent India, the sequential JB gain and FY28-29 direction; management gave only directional H2 'a little higher' commentary.

analyst_focus.topic: Where will the combined India field force settle?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: The 9,100 MR count after merging divisions affects cost and productivity; management said flat this year with a possible 500 addition.

analyst_focus.topic: Is the higher R&D and US filing push sustainable and productive?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: R&D at 4.2% of revenue was above Q1's 3.5%; analysts asked about new investment avenues and US filing cadence, and whether US growth is durable versus price erosion.

analyst_focus.topic: How big and how profitable is India semaglutide, and what about Brazil?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Torrent holds 32% share after a supply gap; analysts asked about market size, pricing per patient and Brazil launch timing, which are key new profit pools.

analyst_focus.topic: Why is Indian pharma market growth suddenly 12%, and will it last?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Market growth is well above recent years; analysts probed GLP-1, trade generics and consolidation as causes. Management could not pinpoint the delta but sees at least 10% next year.

analyst_focus.topic: Is US growth from launches durable?
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: US constant-currency revenue grew 13%; analysts asked how much comes from products with durable advantage. Management said there is no durable advantage in generics; the base is flat and growth comes from new launches.

analyst_focus.topic: Brazil growth drivers and constraints
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Growth was split about equally across price, volume and launches; analysts asked about 53 pending approvals, the constraint (ANVISA timing and local competition) and growth outlook.

analyst_focus.topic: Germany outlook
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Revenue fell about 13% in constant currency; management could offer only a best case of slight decline for coming quarters.

analyst_focus.topic: Curatio and OTC scale-up
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: Curatio is now 7-8% of base India and growing 34%; analysts asked about sustainability and new OTC launches, which are mostly brand extensions.

analyst_focus.topic: JB-Novartis ophthalmology deal risk and payment timing
analyst_focus.why_it_mattered: An analyst asked whether Novartis India changes endanger the deal and when the INR 950-960 cr balance is due; management said the contract is clear and payment is in December.

key_risks: JB international recovery is slower than India and depends on plant-network and QC integration milestones.
R&D at 4-4.5% of revenue for two to three years limits margin expansion even as synergies come through.
New competitors on recent US launches are expected to raise price erosion in H2.
Germany remains weak, with only a best-case outlook of slight decline.
India semaglutide faces rising competition; Q2 shows how supply interruptions can cost share.
A INR 950-960 cr Novartis ophthalmology payment is due in December.

material_guidance_changes.new_guidance: INR 450 cr in about two years
material_guidance_changes.magnitude: Same quantum delivered one year earlier; further upside deferred for a couple of quarters
material_guidance_changes.explicit_statement: Management says synergies are being achieved much faster than planned, in two years instead of three.

evidence.speaker: Aman Mehta
evidence.quote: "But directionally, yes, we've been able to achieve that much faster. Instead of three years, I think we should be able to get there in two years' time."
